newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Five more killed in Karachi violence.
newsitem.headline: Five more killed in Karachi violence.

text.p: Five more people were killed overnight in separate shootings in Pakistan's troubled southern port city of Karachi, police said on Thursday.
The murders followed Wednesday's execution-style shooting of five men who were driven at gunpoint to the Ghaziabad area of Orangi Extension in District West and gunned down in cold blood.
Police said the body of a young man, with marks of torture and bullet wounds, was found at Peerabad in the Gulbahar area of District Central at six a.m. (0100 GMT) on Thursday.
Four men were killed earlier in various attacks, three of them in District Central's Nazimabad area.

Hadi Hasan, a Karachi Municipal Corporation (KMC) engineer, was killed in an ambush, Amjad Hussain, a KMC contractor, was shot dead near his car, and Afaq Ahmed, a driver employed by a government hospital was hit by bullets outside his home.
A fifth man, Salim Butt, 25, was killed outside his house in the Korangi district of District East.
Police said they did not know the motives for any of the killings or the political affiliations of the victims, and there were no immediate claims of responsibility.
Violence has surged in Karachi in recent weeks amid renewed feuding between militants of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) and its MQM-Haqiqi splinter faction.
At least 130 people have died in ethnic, sectarian and political unrest in this sprawling city of 14 million this year, compared to about 500 last year and more than 2,000 in 1995.

The MQM entered a coalition government in Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital, after February 3 elections, but says its alliance with Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League party has failed to bring promised dividends.
